proposals.before: He held Taiping, Kuangguo, Tianping, Zhongwu, Wuning, Guide, and Jinchang in turn. Inns lined the roads wherever he went, and he amassed tens of millions.
proposals.after: He held Taining, Kuangguo, Tianping, Zhongwu, Wuning, Guide, and Jinchang in turn. Inns lined the roads wherever he went, and he amassed tens of millions.
proposals.reason: Chinese 泰寧 is Taining, not Taiping; the idiomatic translation misreads the circuit name.

proposals.before: By dawn he had killed them all. For merit he was made prefect of Cao.
proposals.after: By dawn he had killed them all. For merit he was made prefect of Tan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 澶州 is Tan/Chanzhou; idiomatic wrongly renders it as Cao (曹州).

proposals.before: That year he died at sixty-two, posthumously Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: That year he died at sixty-two, posthumously Grand Marshal.
proposals.reason: Chinese 贈太尉 is Grand Marshal (taiwei), not Grand Preceptor (太師).

decisions.reason: 泰寧 is Taining; Taiping would require 太平.

decisions.after: By dawn he had killed them all. For merit he was made prefect of Chanzhou.
decisions.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Caozhou; spelling out the prefecture avoids the proposal's ambiguous one-syllable form.

decisions.after: That year he died at sixty-two and was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant.
decisions.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor (太師) or Grand Marshal.
